questions.question: It is always possible to draw a circle passing through ______ non-collinear points in a plane.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to fundamental geometric principles, exactly one unique circle can be drawn passing through three non-collinear points.

Any three non-collinear points form a triangle, and the center of the unique circle passing through them is the circumcenter of this triangle.

The circumcenter is geometrically determined by the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides, ensuring it is equidistant from all three vertices.

Hence, 3 non-collinear points are always required and strictly sufficient to define a single circle.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

We need to determine the exact number of non-collinear points required to draw a circle.

**Concept Used:**

A circle is geometrically defined as the locus of all points in a plane that are at an equal distance (radius) from a fixed center point.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

The smallest angle measures 42º less than the greatest angle.

The remaining angle is 24º more than the smallest angle.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180º

**Calculation:**

Let the smallest angle be x º.

Largest angle = x + 42 º

Remaining angle = x + 24° 

Sum of angles: x + (x + 42) + (x + 24) = 180 º

⇒ 3x + 66 = 180

⇒ 3x = 180 - 66

⇒ 3x = 114

⇒ x = 38

Smallest angle = x = 38°. 

**The measure of the smallest angle of the triangle is 38º.**

questions.question: The equation of a straight line on a point (3, -5) and slope 2 is:

questions.question: If two straight lines are coinciding with each other, then the number of points of intersection is/are:

options.text: finite number of point of intersection

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Coinciding lines are two straight lines that lie perfectly on top of each other.

Since a single line is made up of a continuous, infinite series of points, two overlapping lines share every single point.

Thus, they intersect at every point along their entire length.

**∴ The correct answer is infinitely many points of intersection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two straight lines are coinciding with each other.

**Concept Used:**

If two linear equations L₁: a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and L₂: a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 represent coinciding lines, their coefficients are strictly proportional: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Intersecting
 (1 point)

 
 
• 
 
• 
 Parallel
 (0 points)

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 Coinciding
 (Infinite points)

**Calculations:**

⇒ When the equations are proportional, they mathematically represent the exact same straight line.

⇒ A straight line contains an infinitely large set of coordinate points (x, y).

⇒ Because the lines perfectly overlap, every point present on the first line also acts as a point on the second line.

⇒ Therefore, the number of shared (intersecting) points between them is strictly infinite.

**∴ The correct answer is infinitely many points of intersection.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Intersecting Lines

When two lines have completely different slopes (a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂), they will intersect at exactly one unique point, resulting in a single solution.

Parallel Lines

When two lines have the same slope but different intercepts (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂), they never meet each other at any point, resulting in 0 solutions.

Coincident Lines

When two lines share both the same slope and same intercept (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂), they overlap perfectly, resulting in infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: If the graph of the equation 20x + 21y = 420 cuts the coordinate axes at P and Q, then what is the measure of the length (in units) of PQ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The equation of the line is 20x + 21y = 420.

**Formula used:**

To find the intercepts on the axes:

For x-intercept: Put y = 0 in the equation.

For y-intercept: Put x = 0 in the equation.

Distance between two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂):

d = sqrt{(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²}

**Calculation:**

For x-intercept:

20x + 21(0) = 420

⇒ 20x = 420

⇒ x = 21

So, the x-intercept is (21, 0).

For y-intercept:

20(0) + 21y = 420

⇒ 21y = 420

⇒ y = 20

So, the y-intercept is (0, 20).

To find the distance PQ:

d = sqrt{(21 - 0)² + (0 - 20)²}

⇒ d = sqrt{21² + (-20)²}

⇒ d = sqrt{441 + 400}

⇒ d = sqrt{841}

⇒ d = 29

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

Dividing by 60 on both sides,

x-intercept = a = 12

y-intercept = b = 5

The length of the line segment intercepted between the axes is given by the distance between the intercepts:

Length = sqrt{a²+b²}

⇒ Length = sqrt{144+25}

⇒ Length = sqrt{169} = 13 cm

A circle of radius 4 cm is drawn inscribed in a right angle triangle ABC, right angled at C. If AC = 12 cm, then the value of CB is:

The tangent makes a right angle with the radius of a circle at the point of contact.

If two tangents are drawn from an external point of the circle, then they are equal in length.

**Formula used:**

Pythagoras theorem:

H² = P² + B²

Where, P = perpendicular; B = base;

H = hypotenuse

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

⇒ 64 + x² + 16x = 144 + 16 + x² + 8x

⇒ 64 + 16x = 160 + 8x

⇒ x = 96/8 = 12

questions.question: A and B are centres of two circles with radii 2 cm and 1 cm respectively, where AB = 5 cm. C is the centre of another circle of radius r cm, which touches each of the above two circles externally. Iftriangle ACB = 90circ, then the value of r is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If angle ACB = 90°, ΔACB forms a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse AB = 5 cm.

The standard Pythagorean triplet with hypotenuse 5 is (3, 4, 5), so the perpendicular legs must be 3 cm and 4 cm.

The distance between externally touching circles is the sum of their radii, giving AC = r + 2 and BC = r + 1.

By comparing the lengths, setting r = 2 cm directly gives AC = 4 cm and BC = 3 cm.

This perfectly satisfies the right-angled triangle condition without needing to solve quadratic equations.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of circle with centre A = 2 cm

Radius of circle with centre B = 1 cm

Distance between centres A and B (AB) = 5 cm

Circle with centre C touches both circles externally with radius r.

**Formula Used:**

When two circles touch externally, distance between their centres = r₁ + r₂

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance AC = r + 2 cm

⇒ Distance BC = r + 1 cm

Since angle ACB = 90°, ΔACB is a right-angled triangle with AB as the hypotenuse.

⇒ AC² + BC² = AB²

⇒ (r + 2)² + (r + 1)² = 5²

⇒ r² + 4r + 4 + r² + 2r + 1 = 25

⇒ 2r² + 6r + 5 = 25

⇒ 2r² + 6r − 20 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ r² + 3r − 10 = 0

⇒ r² + 5r − 2r − 10 = 0

⇒ r(r + 5) − 2(r + 5) = 0

⇒ (r + 5)(r − 2) = 0

⇒ r = −5 or r = 2

Since the radius of a circle cannot be negative, r = 2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circles Touching Externally

When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii: d = r₁ + r₂.

Circles Touching Internally

When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the absolute difference of their radii: d = |r₁ − r₂|.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers that fit the rule a² + b² = c². Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13) and (8, 15, 17) help solve right-angled triangle problems quickly.

questions.question: Find the equation of the sphere having centre (-1, 2, -3) and the radius of 3 units.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Centre (h, k, l) = (-1, 2, -3)

Radius (r) = 3 units

**Formula used:**

Equation of a sphere: (x - h)² + (y - k)² + (z - l)² = r² 

**Calculation:**

Substitute the given values:

(x + 1)² + (y - 2)² + (z + 3)² = 3²

⇒ (x + 1)² + (y - 2)² + (z + 3)² = 9

Expand and simplify:

(x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1

(y - 2)² = y² - 4y + 4

(z + 3)² = z² + 6z + 9

Combine all terms:

x² + 2x + 1 + y² - 4y + 4 + z² + 6z + 9 = 9

Combine like terms:

⇒ x² + y² + z² + 2x - 4y + 6z + 14 = 9

Subtract 9 from both sides:

⇒ x² + y² + z² + 2x - 4y + 6z + 5 = 0

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The lines x + y = 10 and -3x + y = 2 have a unique solution. What is the distance (in units) between the unique solution and the point of intersection of the line x + y = 10 and the x-axis?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The lines x + y = 10 and -3x + y = 2 have a unique solution.

What is the distance (in units) between the unique solution and the point of intersection of the line x + y = 10 and the x-axis?

**Formula used:**

Distance formula: sqrt{(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²}

**Calculation:**

Solving the system of equations:

x + y = 10 ...(1)

-3x + y = 2 ...(2)

Subtracting (2) from (1):

⇒ x + y - (-3x + y) = 10 - 2

⇒ x + y + 3x - y = 8

⇒ 4x = 8

⇒ x = 2

Substituting x = 2 in (1):

⇒ 2 + y = 10

⇒ y = 8

So, the unique solution is (2, 8).

Point of intersection of x + y = 10 and x-axis:

On the x-axis, y = 0.

⇒ x + 0 = 10

⇒ x = 10

So, the point of intersection is (10, 0).

Using the distance formula:

⇒ Distance = sqrt{(10 - 2)² + (0 - 8)²}

⇒ Distance = sqrt{8² + (-8)²}

⇒ Distance = sqrt{64 + 64}

⇒ Distance = sqrt{128}

⇒ Distance = 8√2

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
